definition.text: A function whose graph lies on or below the straight line joining any two of its points, so the graph is cup-shaped; a concave function is cap-shaped.

facts.text: A twice-differentiable function of one variable is convex exactly when its second derivative is never negative.
Linear functions, quadratics like cx² with c not negative, and exponentials like ceˣ with c not negative are convex.
Convexity makes optimization easier: any local minimum of a convex function is also a global minimum, and a strictly convex function on an open set has at most one minimum.
A function f is convex exactly when its negative, −f, is concave.
Jensen's inequality: a convex function of an average is never more than the average of the convex function's values.
In consumer theory, a diminishing marginal rate of substitution along an indifference curve means preferences are convex.
Demand curves are generally considered convex, in line with diminishing marginal utility.

definition.text: A convex function that curves upward at least as fast as a quadratic, a stronger condition than strict convexity.

facts.text: Every strongly convex function is strictly convex, but not the other way round.
A strongly convex function has a unique global minimum.
x² is strongly convex, while eˣ is strictly but not strongly convex, because its second derivative can come arbitrarily close to zero.

definition.text: A measure of how sensitive a function's output is to a small change in its input; for a single variable it is the slope of the tangent line at a point.

facts.text: It is often described as the instantaneous rate of change, and finding it is called differentiation.
The tangent line it defines is the best straight-line approximation of the function near that point.
Formally, it is the limit of the ratio of change in output to change in input as the input change shrinks to zero.
A function must be continuous at a point to have a derivative there; a step jump has none.
Rules for sums, products and compositions let derivatives of complex functions be built from those of simple ones.
Leibniz notation, dy/dx, was introduced by Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz in 1675.
In economics, short-run marginal cost is the slope, or first derivative, of the variable cost curve.

definition.text: The derivative of a function of several variables with respect to one of them, holding the others fixed.

facts.text: It can be read as the function's rate of change in the direction of that one variable.
Partial derivatives measure change only along the coordinate axes; change in other directions is measured by directional derivatives.
The total derivative gives a complete picture by considering all directions at once.

definition.text: The result of differentiating a function repeatedly: the derivative of the derivative is the second derivative, and so on.

facts.text: The nth derivative is the derivative of the (n−1)th derivative.
The sign of the second derivative tells whether a function is convex: a twice-differentiable function of one variable is convex when it is never negative.

definition.text: A function whose derivative is a given function; it runs differentiation in reverse.

facts.text: Antiderivatives are not unique: adding any constant gives another, because a constant's derivative is zero.
By the fundamental theorem of calculus, the integral of a function over an interval equals the difference of an antiderivative's values at the two ends, giving areas under curves.
